newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 30.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Out with MMP -- voters: Support for the old first past the post voting system is nearly twice that for the MMP system, according to latest polling. Page 1.

Building review due: The select committee considering whether government should build a $94 million building to house ministers should report to Parliament on Tuesday, committee chairman Clem Simich said on Sunday. Page 1.

$448m school upgrade plan: Education Minister Wyatt Creech on Sunday promised $448 million to provide schools with extra facilities but, according to Post Primary Teachers Association, the figure is barely enough to cope with the baby boom of the 1980s. Page 2.

Big price falls unlikely with axing of car tariffs: Car buyers should not expect dramatic changes in prices if the government removes vehicle tariffs completely in three years instead of continuing to phase them out in line with Australia. Page 2.

Government may curb super funds' tax avoidance: The government may change tax rules that allow superannuation funds to avoid tax on capital gains earned through passive investment funds, also called group investment funds. Page 11.

Completion of Defiance sale due this week: The sale of Christchurch-based Defiance Food Industries to Goodman Fielder is expected to be completed this week, according to Defiance chairman Ian White. Page 11.

Tax cuts may be at risk, says Coopers and Lybrand: Winston Peters's first effort as Treasurer has been styled "the mother-in-law of all Budgets" by accountancy firm and consultants Coopers and Lybrand -- "so full of inconsistencies that rather than providing clarity, it fuels uncertainty". Page 12.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Cabinet to face frigate conflict: A committee of senior ministers has suggested buying at least one more $470 million Anzac-class frigate -- but the politically-fraught purchase still has to be agreed upon by a far from united coalition cabinet.

Bosses rate Brash over bland budget: A new exclusive poll of senior executives in the Auckland region has found the great majority believe the coalition government's first budget will have a generally neutral impact on their businesses but does not provide a kickstart either to exports or consumer spending. And the executives rate Reserve Bank governor Don Brash as more important to their businesses than Treasurer Winston Peters.
PM out to boost confidence: The Prime Minister may be on the right path when he tells business to raise its head over the parapet and kickstart the economy into life again.
Govt coal stake under question: THe government will soon consider ways of reducing its investment in Solid Energy, formerly known as Coal Corporation.
Dealers say kiwi will fall: The New Zealand dollar is set for a lower track after Thursday's budget and Friday's Reserve Bank monetary policy statement, offshore foreign exchange dealers say.

Credit rating not affected by lower growth and surpluses: Sovereign credit rating agencies have confirmed New Zealand's rating outlook as stable despite last week's budget and monetary statements indicating lower government surpluses.
Radio network shedding staff in drive to improve profitability: New Zealand's biggest radio company, The Radio Network, is planning to shed more than 130 staff over the next eighteen months.

Telecom prepares for ATM network: Business customers with serious handwidth needs will "later this year" be able to hook up for highspeed data networking when Telecom goes live with its asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) switched network.
THE PRESS
Buck vows to fight Govt power move: Stopping the South Island power differential move has bought the government a fight on all possible fronts, Christchurch Mayor Vicki Buck says.
--Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
